deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a short personal note from 'W. Krause' to a colleague, almost certainly Riemann given its place in the Riemann papers. The archival pencil heading 'Riemann 2' and the folio number '82' are later additions.

The letter is dated 'Gt 5/4 62', i.e. Göttingen, 5 April 1862. Krause apologises for troubling the addressee. Stromeyer, evidently a library official, has told him for the third time that he must return certain books to the (university) library. Krause calls this 'a mere formality', since the books are re-issued straight away. He asks the addressee to send the books back to him, offers to forward them again at once if they are still needed, and mentions that he called once since his return but missed him.

The writer is plausibly Wilhelm Krause (1833–1910), the anatomist, then active in Göttingen; this identification is my inference and is not stated on the page.

The letter only records that Riemann had borrowed library books through a colleague in spring 1862. There are no derivations to reconstruct.

The previous page, a letter from A. Mayer about Gauss and the transformation problem, is unrelated to this one.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a non-mathematical note about returning library books. At most it is a minor biographical datum: borrowed books in Göttingen, April 1862.
transcription_corrections: 'was ja eine reine[?] Form ist': the image supports 'eine reine Form'; the question mark can probably be dropped.
'Gt 5/4 62.' should be read as Göttingen, 5 April 1862.
'Riemann 2' and '82' are later archival pencil annotations, not part of Krause's letter.
